title: Atomic epoch failover controller for stream cohort preservation
creator: Sophie Martinez
description: Problem: Hosted API edge gateways must perform active-active failover without dropping or duplicating in-flight streaming sessions. Existing soft-cutover approaches either sacrifice latency SLOs or lose coherent KV cache state for cohorts of related streams. This ticket proposes an Atomic Epoch Failover Controller (AEFC) that coordinates region-level egress in lockstep using epoch metadata, circuit hold windows, and cohort-aware backpressure to preserve stream continuity and meet SLO targets.
context: We operate multi-region edges with active-active traffic. Streaming sessions maintain server-side KV cache and long-lived connections; naive region failover can cause partial token loss, duplicated responses, or large latency spikes when clients re-establish sessions. We need a mechanism that: (1) defines discrete failover epochs, (2) enables region ingress to drain or hold traffic for particular stream cohorts, (3) orchestrates KV cache salvaging or shadow replication, and (4) integrates with circuit breakers/load-shedding to protect latency SLOs.
proposal_summary: AEFC will introduce an epoch identifier attached to edge sessions. When a region enters a failover window, the controller coordinates a lightweight egress protocol: mark affected cohorts with a 'drain-or-hold' directive, initiate bounded circuit holds (grace windows), optionally shadow-request recent KV slices to the target region, and apply cohort-prioritized hedging or load-shedding to keep median latency within SLO. The approach aims for zero-response-duplication, bounded token preservation, and measurable SLO adherence.
work_updates: 2025-02-10 - Ticket created by Sophie. Initial proposal and constraints captured.
2025-02-11 - Engineering spike: latency impact model for 3s, 10s, 30s drain windows; recommended default 8s circuit hold for streaming cohorts.
2025-02-12 - PM review (Dana Kim): prioritize customer continuity for enterprise streaming customers; flagged KV replication as required for Private deployments.
2025-02-13 - Design feedback (Marta Lopez): suggest cohort hashing by client-token prefix and model-id to reduce cross-cohort blast radius.
2025-02-14 - Assigned to Arjun. Added rollout and QA checklist. Added dependency on ENG-14257 (KV sync primitives).
acceptance_criteria: AEFC implements epoch metadata on edge session lifecycle and propagates it to downstream proxies and runtime nodes.
During a controlled failover drill, 99% of in-flight streaming tokens are either (a) continued with preserved continuity, or (b) failover within the 8s grace window without duplicated responses.
Latency SLO (p95) for streaming append requests degrades by no more than 15% during a failover event in staged rollouts.
Circuit hold and cohort-aware load-shedding triggers are plumbed into the Console (runtime-1.21) and exposed in per-route dashboards.
End-to-end e2e+chaos tests simulate dual-region outage and demonstrate session preservation for small, medium, and large cohorts.
Feature flags exist to toggle AEFC behavior per-customer and per-region; default is opt-in during canary.
Runbook updated with failover playbook and rollback instructions.
risks: KV replication could add write amplification and increase tail latency if not async and bounded; dependency ENG-14257 must deliver lightweight slices.
Incorrect cohort hashing may create hotspots; need sampling analysis during rollout.
Circuit hold windows too long lead to higher error budgets consumed; too short leads to token loss.
Observability gaps: must ensure traces propagate epoch and cohort metadata to link events across regions.
Complex interactions with existing hedging policies may cause double-execution if not gated by epoch checks.
Private deployments with air-gapped constraints may require alternate KV export strategies.
rollout_steps: 1) Feature branch and unit tests for epoch propagation (edge-proxy + gateway).
2) Internal canary across one small region pair with flag enabled for <1% of traffic; collect metrics for 72h.
3) Run targeted chaos test: kill primary region pods and observe session continuity and SLO impact.
4) Expand canary to 5% traffic and enable cohort hashing instrumentation; verify no hotspots.
5) Enable KV slice shadowing for enterprise customers; monitor write amplification.
6) Gradual ramp to global rollout with per-customer opt-in and console controls.
7) Post-rollout: 30-day burn and retrospective; update runbooks and SLAs if needed.
observability_and_metrics: Expose epoch_id and cohort_id as trace tags in OpenTelemetry spans.
New dashboards: epoch-transition rate, session-resume-success-rate, token-duplication-rate, p95/p99 latency during failover windows.
SLOs: streaming-p95 < 250ms baseline, acceptable increase <= 15% during controlled failovers.
Alerting: token-duplication-rate > 0.1% in a 10m window triggers PagerDuty.
Cost metrics: KV shadowing write amplification and added egress per-region.
qa_plan: Unit tests for epoch propagation, circuit hold semantics, and hedging suppression when epoch mismatch detected.
Integration tests for a trio: edge-proxy -> gateway -> runtime with simulated KV slice transfer.
E2E chaos: region kill, network partition, and slow-disk scenarios while asserting acceptance criteria.
Performance benchmark before/after enabling AEFC at 1%, 5%, 20% traffic to measure tail latency impact.
Security review for epoch metadata exposure in logs; ensure masking for PII-sensitive identifiers.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-12: default grace window set to 8s (configurable per-route), based on spike analysis.
Decision 2025-02-13: cohort hashing strategy = (model-id, client-id-prefix) to balance locality and blast radius.
Tradeoff: enabling aggressive KV shadowing improves continuity but increases cost — plan to gate behind enterprise surcharge.
Follow-up: implement a telemetry-driven auto-tuner for hold-window length based on epoch-transition success rates.
